# Taxottic

> Taxottic is tax-forecasting software for freelancers, independent contractors, sole proprietors, and small businesses in the United States. It connects to your bank, keeps a running quarterly estimated-tax forecast in step with your income, and surfaces IRS-cited deductions, so self-employed filers can set money aside before it's due and claim everything they're legally owed. Made by Techno Optics LLC. Lives at https://taxottic.com.

Taxottic ("tax" + the "-ottic" suffix it shares with its sibling product Advottic) turns the once-a-year scramble of self-employment taxes into a calm, always-current picture. Instead of guessing at quarter-end, you see what you'll likely owe today and how each deduction changes it.

What it does:
- Bank-synced quarterly estimated-tax forecasts (federal + state) that update as money moves
- A catalog of 1,025 IRS-cited deductions, each linked to its IRC section and IRS publication
- Automatic Schedule C assembly with PDF export for your CPA
- Multi-state forecasting, QBI (Qualified Business Income) math, and AMT detection
- Quarterly estimated-tax reminders so you never miss a due date
- Automatic business-mileage tracking (phone + Wear OS watch) at the IRS standard rate
- Receipt and document OCR via its built-in assistant, "Bella"
- Tax year 2026 with OBBBA (One Big Beautiful Bill Act) amendments

Who it's for: self-employed people and small businesses (1099 contractors, freelancers, gig workers, sole proprietors, single-member LLCs, S-corps) and the accounting firms that serve them. It is a forecasting and organization tool, not a filing service, and not a substitute for advice from a licensed CPA or tax attorney.

Availability: Taxottic runs in any web browser and is available as a native mobile app for download on both the Apple App Store (iPhone and iPad) and the Google Play Store (Android phones and tablets). Use it free at https://taxottic.com or install the app on your phone.

## Guides
Long-form explainers on United States self-employment tax. Each cites the
relevant IRC section or IRS publication.
- [How much should I set aside for taxes when self-employed?](https://taxottic.com/guides/self-employment-tax-how-much-to-set-aside): Sizing the set-aside from self-employment tax (15.3%) plus federal and state income tax, and why 25-30% of net income is a common starting point.
- [Schedule C deductions: what self-employed people can write off](https://taxottic.com/guides/schedule-c-deductions): The everyday business expenses freelancers and sole proprietors can deduct, home office, mileage, software, phone, supplies, retirement, and health insurance, each tied to its IRS source.
- [Quarterly estimated taxes, explained](https://taxottic.com/guides/quarterly-estimated-taxes-explained): Who owes them, the four due dates, how to estimate each payment, and how the safe-harbor rule avoids the IRS underpayment penalty.
- [Business mileage deduction: how to track and claim it](https://taxottic.com/guides/business-mileage-deduction): The standard mileage rate versus actual vehicle expenses, which drives count, and the mileage log the IRS expects you to keep.
- [Home office deduction: who qualifies and how to calculate it](https://taxottic.com/guides/home-office-deduction): The "regular and exclusive use" test, and how the simplified ($5/sq ft) and actual-expense methods compare.
- [1099 vs W-2: how each affects your taxes](https://taxottic.com/guides/1099-vs-w2): Who withholds, who pays self-employment tax, who can deduct expenses, and who owes quarterly estimates.
- [Your first year freelancing: a tax checklist](https://taxottic.com/guides/first-year-freelancer-tax-checklist): Set aside money, separate your finances, track deductions, and pay quarterly estimates.
- [The QBI deduction: a 20% break for small-business income](https://taxottic.com/guides/qbi-deduction): Who qualifies, how the income limits and the specified-service-business phase-out work, and how it lowers taxable income.
- [Sole proprietor, LLC, or S-corp: how each is taxed](https://taxottic.com/guides/sole-proprietor-vs-llc-vs-s-corp-taxes): Pass-through income, self-employment tax, and when an S-corp salary-plus-distributions setup can save money.
- [The self-employed health insurance deduction](https://taxottic.com/guides/self-employed-health-insurance-deduction): Who qualifies, what counts, and why it is an adjustment to income rather than a Schedule C expense.
- [What is a 1099-K? Thresholds and what to do with it](https://taxottic.com/guides/what-is-a-1099-k): What it reports, why payment apps send one, the changing reporting threshold, and how to reconcile it.
- [All guides](https://taxottic.com/guides): The full index.

## Calculators
Free, no sign-up, no account. Each runs the same IRS-aligned engine as the
product itself.
- [Self-employment tax calculator](https://taxottic.com/calculators/self-employment-tax): Estimate 2026 self-employment tax (15.3%), federal and state income tax, the QBI deduction, and quarterly payments from 1099 income.
- [1099 tax calculator](https://taxottic.com/calculators/1099-tax): For independent contractors, gig workers, and freelancers. Tax on 1099-NEC and 1099-K income, federal plus state, QBI, and quarterly payments.
- [Quarterly estimated tax calculator](https://taxottic.com/calculators/quarterly-estimated-tax): All four 2026 IRS due dates, federal plus state, self-employment tax, and QBI.
- [How much to set aside for taxes](https://taxottic.com/calculators/how-much-to-set-aside): The exact percentage of every payment to hold back, covering self-employment tax plus federal and state income tax.
- [Mileage deduction calculator](https://taxottic.com/calculators/mileage-deduction): Deduction and estimated tax savings from business miles at the 2026 IRS standard mileage rate.
- [Effective tax rate calculator](https://taxottic.com/calculators/effective-tax-rate): Effective rate, marginal bracket, total tax, and after-tax take-home, for W-2 or self-employment income.
- [All calculators](https://taxottic.com/calculators): The full index, including per-state and per-income-amount versions of the self-employment tax calculator.
